instruction: Add a new slide at the end of this presentation with the title 'Resources' and save the file.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened terminal, installed python-pptx and python-docx, wrote a Python script to extract all slide text to a Word document. First attempt failed with XML compatibility error due to control characters in presentation. Second attempt with text cleaning also failed. Model got stuck in a response loop.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, run shell commands, install pip packages, write Python scripts, interact with LibreOffice Impress GUI
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to create script.docx because python-docx threw ValueError on control characters (\x0b) in the presentation text. The regex cleaning pattern was incorrectly escaped in the heredoc. Model then got stuck in an infinite </think> loop.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified from multi-app text extraction to a single Impress operation (adding a slide), which stays within the same application and avoids cross-format character encoding issues
metadata.explanation: Task asks to add a new slide at the end with title 'Resources'. Evaluator uses a custom getter to read the PPTX, count slides, and get the last slide title. Metric gives 0.5 for correct slide count (29) and 0.5 for correct last slide title. Postconfig saves the file before evaluation.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the PPTX file, counts slides, and extracts the last slide's title text
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (proper handling for type='rule')
Both instruction requirements are verified: new slide added (count >= 29) and title is 'Resources' (case-insensitive)
Postconfig properly saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring file state is fresh
Partial credit scoring (0.5 count + 0.5 title) is reasonable for this two-requirement task
Minor: getter uses first text shape as title rather than checking for title placeholder specifically, which could be imprecise if other shapes precede the title
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using shape.placeholder_format to identify the title placeholder instead of taking the first text shape, for more robust title extraction
